newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's Alphatec says wants government help.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's Alphatec says wants government help.

text.p: Thai electronics giant Alphatec Group expects the government to provide an investment of up to $70 million after Texas Instruments Inc withdrew from two joint ventures, senior executives said on Friday.

Charn Uswachoke, chairman of the group, told reporters the state-run National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC) was likely to buy a 25 percent stake in Alpha-TI Semiconductors Co Ltd.
Texas Instruments of the United States held the stake in the company before announcing it was pulling out on Thursday.
"We expect to get around $50 million from NECTEC (for Alpha-TI). But we cannot reveal the details now as it could ruin the whole situation," he said.
NECTEC is also expected to buy a 10 percent stake of another, unrelated major Alphatec project -- Submicron Technology Plc. The venture is Thailand's first silicon-chip foundry.
Alphatec Group Chief Operating Officer Bob Mollerstuen said the 10 percent equity acquisiton would cost NECTEC around $20 million.
"I can't tell you how imminent the deal is. When you deal with the government, it is very difficult to say...But they are very positive," Mollerstuen told Reuters.

Charn also urged the government to provide more support to the electronics and other high-technology industries to help Thailand sustain its export competitiveness as labour-intensive products are losing market share to lower-wage countries.
"In many countries such as Singapore and South Korea, the government provides necessary support for this kind of industry," he said.

"The Thai government must step in to help the industry. It cannot afford not to as the country's economic future depends on higher-end products and not lower-end products such as textiles. Moreover, the demand for electronics is still growing," Charn said.
A slowdown in the Thai economy and the depressed stock market have crippled Alphatec Group's ability to raise funds to finance its projects.

U.S.-based Texas Instruments on Thursday said it had terminated joint venture agreements in Alpha-TI Semiconductors and Alpha Memory Co Ltd, citing Alphatec's inability to finance the project in the time frame required.

Texas Instruments holds a 25 percent stake in Alpha-TI Semiconductors, which was established in December 1995 to produce 16- and 64-megabit DRAMs, and 49 percent of Alpha Memory, which was intended as an assembly and test facility.
Under the agreements, Alphatec Group, which had already invested $100 million in the Alpha-TI project, needed to come up with another $100 million by last Friday.
"The financial market situation makes it difficult to meet the deadline. Texas Instruments does not allow us to bring in new partners," said Leslie Merszei, Alphatec Group's chief financial officer.

Alphatec Group must now first buy Texas Instruments' stake in the two joint ventures, paying around $20 million for the stake in Alpha-TI and about $5 million for Alpha Memory. The payments were to be made in 12 installments over a year.
It was unclear why NECTEC was being asked for $50 million when Alphatec needed to spend only $25 million for the two stakes.
Charn said the group would have no difficulty buying the stakes, which will then be sold to a new partner or partners. Besides NECTEC, he said talks were under way with one major U.S. company.
